craft_notes: Sthāyin: day-by-day ripening (ekayoga + dine dine — the one-yoking practiced daily). Rows: row 2 (day-to-day→fullness). Close: fullness (pūrṇatā — the full-word lands; utter kept as its intensifier). Rejected: 'practice makes perfect' — killed: day to day kept (the patience IS the method); 'samadhi' — killed: full-formed state kept (the verse's own fruit-name).

lines: Here in one-yoking standing, from day to day:
full-formed state — contentment here, utter fullness.
l4.sanskrit_cite: atraikatamayuktisthe yotpadyeta dinād dinam | bharitākāratā sātra tṛptir atyantapūrṇatā

reads_against.argmap: What arises from practice? → Day by day in the one-yoking, full-formed state ripens to utter fullness.
c1_essence: One-yoking day by day: full-formed state, utter fullness.
reads_against.c1_rasa: vīra with śānta (resolve closing the practice arc)
